scenario.name: recovery-expense:v1 direct-security-recovery driftwood
scenario.note: Separate institution-year direct recovery-expense planning model. No empirical calibration or control-effectiveness credit. Delegated prospective institution-year planning policy, not measured frequency: use a common PERT annual incident-frequency range [0.25, 1, 3] for incidents with eligible recovery activity incurred during 2027, including carry-in. One incident/year is a planning reserve reference; lower/upper parameters are chosen uncertainty bounds, not evidence-derived rates or a real-world cap. No workload contingencies were summed, no known/future outcomes were fitted, and identical policy across the three institutions does not establish independent incidents. Delegated prospective per-incident within-year expense budget, not measured staffing/payroll/loss: planned incremental labour [10, 40, 160] hours at an explicitly adopted GBP100/hour charge-out rule plus illustrative incremental vendor/restoration allowances [0, 1000, 4000] GBP gives PERT [1000, 5000, 20000] GBP. Forty hours is one planning work-week of aggregate recovery capacity, never a statement about employee count or available staff. These are distribution parameters, not quantiles, invoice forecasts or actual-expense caps. Count only eligible expense incurred within 2027; no carry-out, routine operating cost, lost sales/fines/premiums/customer losses or control-effectiveness credit.

unit.basis: nominal direct security-incident recovery expense per registered subject-year
